chunks: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, who is singular in oneness and alone in divinity. He originated the servants upon His recognition, rendered tongues unable to describe Him, and veiled eyes from seeing Him. He is exalted above the attributes of created beings and too majestic for the meanings of the limited. There is no likeness to Him among all creatures, and there is no god other than Him for all the worlds. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, a testimony of one confessing His tawhid, desiring His generosity, and repenting from his sins.

And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. He chose him for His message, entrusted to him the landmarks of His religion, and sent him with His Book as a proof over His servants. And I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib is his wasi and the best of creation after him, the one who undertakes his command and calls to his path, and that he is Amir al-Mu'minin, the master of the wasis, and the worthiest of people with the Prophets; and that his wife Fatimah al-Zahra is the lady of the women of the worlds; and that al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and the Imams [the nine] from his offspring are the Imams of guidance, the standards of taqwa, and Allah's proofs over the people of the world. And I bear witness that whoever follows them is saved, and whoever lags behind them is ruined. May Allah's blessings, mercy, and benedictions be upon them, their souls, and their bodies.

To proceed: I found that my shaykhs and forefathers—may Allah have mercy on them—compiled books in the various branches of knowledge, yet neglected composing a book that includes numbered categories and praiseworthy and blameworthy traits. I found much benefit in compiling it for the seeker of knowledge and the one desirous of good, so I sought nearness to Allah, majestic is His Name, by composing this book, seeking His reward and desiring success through His mercy. And I hope that He will not disappoint me regarding what I have aspired to and hoped from Him through His gracious bounty and favor. Indeed, He is powerful over all things.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الْهُدَىٰ: the Imams who lead to guidance
key_terms.الْخِصَالِ: qualities or traits, especially praiseworthy and blameworthy characteristics
key_terms.الْوَحْدَانِيَّةِ: absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah
key_terms.رِسَالَتِهِ: the divine messengership entrusted to Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: his designated successor and testamentary trustee

ai.seo_question: What does the introduction to al-Khisal say about tawhid, prophethood, and the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This introduction opens with praise of Allah and a confession of tawhid, followed by testimony to the رسالَة of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It then explains the author's purpose in compiling the book: to gather beneficial material on numbered virtues and vices for seekers of knowledge, seeking nearness to Allah and His reward.
